description: Communication frameworks, document structures, and writing best practices from McKinsey, BCG, and Bain for executive-level business documents.

answerFirst.principle: Lead with the conclusion, then provide supporting evidence
answerFirst.rationale: Executives are time-constrained; they want the answer immediately
answerFirst.badExample: We analyzed 47 data points across 12 regions over 5 years and conducted 23 interviews...
answerFirst.goodExample: We recommend pursuing Strategy A, which will increase EBITDA by 15% at acceptable risk...

soWhat.principle: Every piece of analysis must answer 'So what?' - the implication or action
soWhat.test: If removed, would the decision-maker care?
soWhat.goodExample: Market share loss of 4pts translates to $12M revenue at risk; requires immediate pricing response

threeRule.principle: Group ideas in threes for memorability and structure
threeRule.rationale: Three is cognitively optimal for retention and persuasion

actionOrientation.principle: Every document should drive to specific, actionable recommendations
actionOrientation.avoidance: Analysis for analysis' sake; no 'findings' without 'implications'

executiveSummary.purpose: Standalone synopsis for senior executives who may not read full report

situation.example: CompanyX operates in a $2B widget market growing at 5% annually. Despite market leadership, profitability has declined 300bps over 3 years.

complication.example: New entrants with 20% cost advantage have captured 8pts of market share. CompanyX's cost structure is no longer competitive.

question.example: How can CompanyX restore margins while defending market position?

answer.example: We recommend a three-pronged transformation: 1) Reduce COGS by $40M through manufacturing consolidation, 2) Shift product mix to premium segments, 3) Selective price increases in low-elasticity segments.

example: Manufacturing consolidation: Close 2 of 5 plants, invest in automation → $40M annual savings by Year 2
Premium shift: Launch 3 new products in high-margin segments → +500bps margin by Year 3
Pricing: 5-8% increases in segments with elasticity <-0.8 → $15M revenue, minimal volume loss

implications.example: This program will restore EBITDA margins to 18% (vs. 14% today) and deliver $60M value in 3 years. Board approval needed by Q2 to achieve Year 1 savings targets.

formatting.emphasis: Bold for key numbers and recommendations

slideDeck.purpose: Visual presentation for meetings, steering committees, or board presentations

structure: Title with key message
3-4 supporting insights with visuals
Clear recommendation at bottom
1pager.usage: Weekly updates, steering committees, quick decisions

pitchDeck.purpose: Sell a strategy, project, or investment
structure: Situation (1-2 slides): Context and market landscape
Complication (2-3 slides): The problem/opportunity
Solution (5-8 slides): Your recommendation with supporting analysis
Implementation (2-3 slides): How to execute, timeline, resources
Next Steps (1 slide): Clear actions, owners, dates
Executive Summary (1 slide)
Progress vs Plan (2-3 slides): Milestones, KPIs, deliverables
Issues & Risks (2-4 slides): Blockers, mitigations
Deep Dive (5-10 slides): Detail on key workstreams
Decisions Needed (2-3 slides): Clear asks of steering committee
Next Period Priorities (1 slide)
Exec Summary (1 slide): The ask and key points
Strategic Context (2-3 slides): Industry, competitive, financial performance
Recommendation (5-10 slides): Options considered, recommended approach, supporting analysis
Financial Impact (2-3 slides): NPV, IRR, sensitivity, funding
Risk & Mitigation (2 slides): Key risks and how you'll address them
Next Steps (1 slide): Timeline, governance, Board actions needed

title.goodExample: Market share declined 4pts in Q3, driven by pricing pressure in Segment A

content.textLimit: 6 bullet points max, 6 words per bullet guideline ('6x6 rule')
content.visualPriority: Chart > Table > Text (always prefer visual over text)
content.whitespace: 40-50% of slide should be empty (avoid clutter)

layout.colors: Brand colors only, max 4 colors per slide

navigation.agenda: Include agenda slide for >15 slide decks
navigation.appendix: Move supporting detail to appendix, reference in main deck

fullReport.purpose: Comprehensive written report for detailed documentation

executiveSummary.standalone: Must be understandable without reading full report

appendices.organization: Lettered (Appendix A, B, C) and titled
appendices.reference: Referenced from main body with [See Appendix A]

writingStyle.tense: Present tense for findings, future for recommendations
writingStyle.jargon: Minimize; define acronyms on first use
writingStyle.numbers: Spell out one through nine, numerals for 10+

body.opening: Lead with the recommendation or key message (1 paragraph)
body.close: Next steps and call to action (1 paragraph)

example.re: Recommendation to accelerate Phase 2 implementation to Q3 2026
example.opening: We recommend accelerating Phase 2 from Q4 to Q3 to capture $5M in savings 3 months earlier and align with FY budget cycle.
example.support: Three key drivers: 1) Vendor capacity is available now but uncertain in Q4, 2) Early benefits fund Phase 3, 3) Aligns with CFO's budget planning timeline.
example.close: Request approval by Friday to secure vendor slot. Implementation team is prepared to start Week of March 15.

oneSlider.name: One-Slide Summary ('Slide Zero')
oneSlider.purpose: Standalone summary that precedes a longer deck

structure.title: Full sentence with key message/recommendation
structure.topRight: Visual supporting the recommendation (chart or diagram)

oneSlider.usage: Board meetings (execs read this first), steering committees, project approvals

structure.purpose: Introduce the problem that disrupts the situation

example.situation: CompanyX has maintained 30% market share for a decade in a stable $500M market.
example.complication: However, three new digital-native competitors entered in 2025, offering 20% lower prices through direct-to-consumer models. CompanyX lost 5pts share in 6 months.
example.resolution: We recommend a dual strategy: 1) Launch direct channel to match new entrants, 2) Differentiate legacy channel with premium services justifying current prices. This will stabilize share at 28% and protect 90% of current revenue.

problemSolutionBenefit.name: Problem-Solution-Benefit

structure.content: Current state pain points, quantified impact
What we will do differently, how it works

problemSolutionBenefit.emphasis: Heavy emphasis on benefits (WIIFM - What's In It For Me)

before.description: Paint picture of current state problems

transition.description: Roadmap showing how to get from before to after

3act.name: Three-Act Structure

acts.name: Conflict
acts.content: Present challenges, obstacles, alternative approaches considered

3act.usage: Case studies, transformation narratives, strategic storytelling

clarity.sentenceLength: 15-20 words average (vary for rhythm, but avoid >30 words)

activeVoice.bad: The project was completed by the team

wordiness.bad: In order to optimize the utilization of resources

fillerWords.exception: Acceptable in casual communication, remove in formal documents

persuasion.evidenceBased: Support every claim with data, cite sources
persuasion.quantification: Numbers are more persuasive than words (23% > 'significant')
persuasion.comparisons: Use benchmarks, alternatives, or past performance for context
persuasion.callToAction: Every document should end with clear next steps and owners

scannability.goal: Reader can skim and grasp key points in 30 seconds

lists.bullets: For unordered items or short lists
lists.numbers: For sequential steps or prioritized items
lists.parallelStructure: Start each bullet with same part of speech (all verbs or all nouns)

currency.multiple: EGP 4.5M ($96K USD) - show both if relevant

indexing.purpose: Show trends when absolute values are less important
indexing.method: Set base year = 100, calculate others as (Value / Base Value) × 100

benchmarking.visualization: Bar chart with reference line for benchmark

order.descending: By value (highest to lowest) unless natural order exists
order.natural: Time (left to right), geography (alphabetical or logical), process (sequential)

simplification.aggregation: Group small items into 'Other' category if <5% each

content: Clear recommendation or answer stated upfront
So what?' answered for each section
Next steps are specific (who, what, when)
structure: Logical flow (SCQA or similar)
MECE organization (no gaps or overlaps)
Headings create clear hierarchy
Transitions between sections
Consistent numbering/formatting
design: Professional appearance (no clipart, comic sans, etc.)

avoid: Burying the lead (answer on page 5 instead of page 1)
Chart titles that just describe ('Revenue by Year' instead of 'Revenue grew 15% CAGR')
Passive voice ('It was decided' instead of 'We recommend')
Vague recommendations ('Improve customer satisfaction' instead of 'Reduce call wait times to <2 min by Q3')
Analysis without implication ('Share dropped 5pts' without 'costing us $10M annually')
Too much text on slides (>50 words)

templateIntegration.withDOCX: Use createHeading, createParagraph, createTable from Omega_DOCX_Template_Standards_v1.1.0.json
templateIntegration.withVISUALS: Reference BIG3_VISUALIZATION_LIBRARY.json for chart types and design
templateIntegration.withFRAMEWORKS: Apply frameworks from BIG3_CONSULTING_FRAMEWORKS.json in analysis sections
templateIntegration.consistency: Maintain same narrative pattern throughout document (don't mix SCQA with Problem-Solution)
